title: Adaptive Graph Learning for Efficient Thermal Analysis of Multi-Stacking Chiplet Systems under Interface Variations
problem: Thermal analysis of 2.5D/3D chiplet systems with multiple stacking layers requires expensive FEM simulations. Interface variations add complexity and computational burden.
motivation: Multi-chiplet systems need rapid, accurate thermal prediction to enable efficient power management and design optimization.
method: The method combines graph neural networks (AI models that map connections between components) with finite element simulation (dividing the chiplet stack into sections to calculate heat flow). A key technique is adaptive graph learning, which adjusts predictions based on the specific thermal properties at each layer's interface. This hybrid approach achieves 1000× faster predictions than traditional finite difference methods, with 0.05% mean absolute percentage error accuracy.
key_novelty: The innovation is using graph neural networks combined with finite element simulation to automatically adapt thermal predictions for stacked chiplets based on how each interface conducts heat differently.
limitations: Limited to thermal analysis; generalization to other physics simulations and different chiplet architectures not discussed.
